title: Profile guardian signoff, staged stability windows, and rollback orchestration
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: implement a guardian signoff and staged stability window system for Redwood-verified performance profiles so that new or updated profiles can be published with explicit cross-functional approval, automated stability measurement, and an orchestrated rollback path if quality or economics regressions are detected.

Why: current publish flows are largely automated and rely on ad-hoc canaries and manual rollbacks. We need a reproducible, auditable publish contract that combines: (1) an automated smoke verification suite, (2) a short, enforced stability window with graduated traffic ramp, (3) a guardian (PM/Eng/QA) signoff step for any profile pin or major version publish, and (4) a runbook-driven rollback orchestration that can be executed automatically on threshold breaches or manually with one-click. This reduces customer-facing regressions and speeds safe rollouts.

Scope and acceptance criteria: 
- Design and store a signed publish manifest for each verified profile that includes profile fingerprint, sample workload, regional anchors, cost estimate, and stability-rule set.
- Implement a guardian_signoff_state in the publish pipeline: draft -> guarded -> active. Transition to active requires at least one guardian approval and passing automated smoke check.
- Create staged stability windows: 5% traffic (1 hour), 25% (6 hours), 100% (24 hours) configurable per release.
- Integrate metric checks for latency p95, avg throughput, and cost-per-token delta vs baseline. Breach thresholds should be configurable per profile.
- Implement rollback orchestration: automated rollback trigger (metric breaches), safe rollback path to previous pinned profile, and an audit trail. Rollback must preserve model pin history and annotate the manifest with reason.
- Provide console UI for guardians to review smoke test artifacts, approve/deny, and trigger manual rollback.
- Document runbook and on-call playbook for false positives and regional anomalies.

Implementation notes: 
- Use existing verification harness (PM-314159) for smoke tests and canonical sample sets; extend harness to produce signed attestations stored in the manifest S3 registry.
- Rely on runtime's existing rollback APIs in runtime-1.20; add an orchestration layer to sequence traffic ramps and rollbacks with idempotency keys.
- Observability: surface per-stage metrics in Console (canary window charts, rollback triggers, timeline). Add a per-profile health badge.
- Security: manifests must be signed with KMS key; guardian approvals logged to audit with SSO identity.

Risks and trade-offs: 
- Longer time-to-publish due to manual signoffs; mitigate by enabling trusted automated guardians for low-risk profile edits.
- Complexity of regional divergence (different anchors may pass in one region but fail in another) — initial implementation will default to global fail-on-breach and add regional relaxations later.

Stakeholders: PM (Sofia Martinez), Runtime Eng (Liam Chen, Priya Kapoor), QA (Marcus Yi), Console (Elena Novak), Security (Ravi Singh).

Acceptance tests: 
- End-to-end test that creates a draft manifest, runs smoke tests, obtains guardian approval, ramps traffic, and completes without triggers.
- Failure test: inject artificial latency to breach threshold at 25% stage and assert automated rollback to previous pinned profile and audit annotation.

Rollout plan: 
1) Feature flag behind verified-profiles.guardian_release.
2) Alpha: internal teams only with 2 sample profiles for 2 weeks.
3) Beta: selected customers and automated guardians for low-risk models.
4) GA: enable for all profile publishes with self-serve opt-out for non-pinned experimental uploads (30 days after beta).
